item.title: SpiceJet launches special flights from Fujairah in UAE to India to help stranded travellers amid Iran vs US-Israel war
item.description: Amidst Iran vs US-Israel war travel chaos, SpiceJet launched special flights from Fujairah in UAE to India, aiding hundreds stranded by regional tensions. This move highlights the vital India-Gulf air corridor's resilience and airlines' swift adaptation to geopolitical crises. The emergency services, utilising Fujairah as a less congested hub, are crucial in clearing travel backlogs and reconnecting the regions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Robots that can tow 500kg: Dubai deploys AI-powered drones, aquatic rescue bots on beaches to enhance coastal safety
item.description: Dubai is enhancing beach safety with new technology. Aquatic rescue robots and aerial drones are now assisting lifeguards. This system helps respond faster to emergencies at sea. The robots can reach swimmers quickly and tow them to safety. Drones provide aerial surveillance and deliver flotation devices. This integrated approach aims to prevent drowning and improve rescue efficiency for beachgoers.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

Meet Aman Gottumukkala: Indian-origin founder joining xAI after building a million-dollar startup with just a three-person team
item.description: Aman Gottumukkala, an Indian-origin engineer, is joining Elon Musk's xAI. He previously founded Firebender, an AI coding assistant for Android developers. This startup reportedly earned millions with a team of just three. Gottumukkala's move highlights a new era where small teams leverage AI to build successful products. He will now focus on advanced coding AI systems at xAI.

item.title: UAE offers free Fazaa membership in ‘Year of Family 2026’: Who can apply
item.description: UAE residents with children are set to receive free Fazaa memberships in 2026, a move by the government to boost social cohesion and ease living costs. This initiative, part of the 'Year of the Family,' offers extensive discounts on retail, dining, travel and entertainment, recognising families' contributions and fostering community well-being.

item.title: Tucker Carlson says CIA accessed his messages, tried to frame him as foreign agent
item.description: Tucker Carlson alleges the CIA is recommending the Justice Department charge him as an unregistered foreign agent for Iran, claiming they read his texts. He insists his communications were journalistic and denies acting against US interests. Carlson suggests the probe is politically motivated due to his views on Israel and the war.

item.title: 'Misleading claims': UAE official rebukes Iranian top minister, rejects aggression accusation amid Iran vs US-Israel war
item.description: A sharp diplomatic row has erupted between the United Arab Emirates and Iran. Iran accused the UAE of aggression, a claim the UAE strongly denies. Emirati officials state their actions are purely defensive. The region faces heightened instability due to ongoing Iran vs US-Israel war. The UAE emphasises restraint and diplomacy while protecting its territory and citizens.

item.title: 500 Golden Visa holders return to UAE after being stranded abroad: Authorities step up crisis response amid Iran vs US-Israel war
item.description: Amidst Iran vs US-Israel war travel chaos, the UAE has successfully repatriated nearly 500 Golden Visa holders and residents stranded abroad due to airspace closures. This swift action highlights the nation's robust emergency response and flexible immigration policies, ensuring the safety and well-being of expatriates during geopolitical uncertainty. The initiative underscores the UAE's commitment to its international community.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Shame on you’: Protest outside Zara after girl attacked by group in UK's Bristol
item.description: Protesters targeted a Bristol Zara store after a brutal attack on a teenage girl on March 4. The victim, filmed during the assault, sought refuge in the store before being attacked outside. Five teenagers have been arrested and released on bail. The girl's father expressed distress over the lack of intervention from bystanders.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum announces new law for Police Academy: 5-year service rule, new degrees, AI training and more
item.description: Dubai has enacted a new law to modernise its Police Academy, aiming to enhance policing through technology and advanced training. The legislation establishes a new governance structure, expands academic programs to include digital transformation and mandates a five-year service commitment for graduates. This initiative reinforces Dubai's commitment to maintaining its status as a global leader in safety and innovation.

item.title: 'Only defending our people': Iran dismisses Trump's claim on 'wanting a deal', says 'no reason for talks'
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed Donald Trump's claims of seeking a deal, stating Iran has no reason to talk with Americans due to past "negative experiences". He asserted Iran's strength and that they're only "defending its people", while also noting countries are negotiating for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: ‘I’m not a secret Nazi’: Graham Platner defends controversial tattoo, says critics misunderstood it
item.description: Maine Senate candidate Graham Platner has changed his stance on a controversial tattoo. He now states he no longer apologizes for the symbol, which resembled a Nazi emblem. Platner claims Jewish leaders understood his explanation after he shared his story. He previously said he got the tattoo in Croatia while inebriated and did not know its Nazi connection.
